subject.title: [Bug]: agents set-identity --workspace does not set the agent's stored workspace, but its success response implies it does

question: Should the public CLI solve existing-agent workspace relocation with a new dedicated setter/update command, or only clarify that `set-identity --workspace` is a locator and adjust the response shape?
rationale: Both repairs are technically plausible, but the choice changes public CLI semantics and JSON compatibility, so maintainer product intent is needed before a fix PR.

options.title: Add Dedicated Setter
options.body: Add `agents set-workspace` or `agents update --workspace` using the existing Gateway update path, and make `set-identity` output explicit about locator versus stored workspace.

options.title: Clarify Locator Only
options.body: Keep relocation out of the CLI for now and add additive output/docs wording so `set-identity` cannot be read as confirming a stored workspace update.

options.title: Repurpose Set Identity
options.body: Make `set-identity --workspace` update stored workspace too, accepting the compatibility risk against current help text and docs.

recommendation.title: Add Dedicated Setter
recommendation.body: Add `agents set-workspace` or `agents update --workspace` using the existing Gateway update path, and make `set-identity` output explicit about locator versus stored workspace.

likelyOwner.reason: The original identity helper and public CLI shape trace to this owner, and this is primarily a CLI contract decision.
